title: Add parallel.ai feature parity case study and cross-repository issue plan (issue #29)
body:
Fixes #29

## Summary

Issue #29 asks for a deep case study of parallel.ai, a complete list of requirements with solution plans, and a dependency-ordered set of issues for both `web-search` (search) and `web-capture` (fetching). This PR is documentation-only.

- `docs/case-studies/issue-29/README.md`: scope checklist, the six requirements of the issue with alternatives and selected plans, a verified inventory of every parallel.ai product (Search, Image Search, Extract, Task, Responses, Chat, FindAll, Entity Search, Monitor, Memory, webhooks, source policy, integrations, crawler) with inputs, outputs, latency, pricing, quotas and the local doc file for each claim, the current capability map of both repositories, a gap analysis that assigns each feature to a repository and a draft issue, per-feature solution alternatives with candidate libraries for JS and Rust, a mermaid dependency graph, a phased delivery order, and assumptions.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-29/issues/`: 26 ready-to-file issue drafts (`web-search-01…18`, `web-capture-01…08`), each with front matter (`id`, `repo`, `title`, `depends_on`, `labels`), summary, scope, acceptance criteria, and references.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-29/data/`: issue #29 and comments, issue lists of both repositories, the web-capture README, and the full public parallel.ai documentation snapshot (111 pages, OpenAPI 3.1 spec, `llms.txt`, agent skill) downloaded on 2026-10-07.
- `experiments/issue-29/download-parallel-docs.sh`: reproducible download of the snapshot.
- `experiments/issue-29/file-issues.sh`: files the drafts with `gh issue create` and links dependencies; it is a dry run unless `--apply` is passed.

## Issues were drafted, not filed

Creating 26 issues across two repositories is an outward-facing action, so the drafts are left for a maintainer to review and file with one command:

```bash
bash experiments/issue-29/file-issues.sh --apply
```

## Validation

- Download finished with `downloaded=111 failed=0`; the OpenAPI spec parses (37 operations, 183 schemas).
- A script checked that all 26 drafts reference only known ids and that the dependency graph is acyclic.
- The filing script dry run lists all 26 drafts and their dependencies without creating anything.
- Prettier passes on the new markdown; `data/` is excluded by `.prettierignore`.
- No code changes, so no changeset or Rust changelog fragment is needed.

title: Expose no_std merging and registry; enforce dependency freshness
body:
Consumers currently cannot reuse the Rust merger and provider catalog in `no_std` environments, and the direct tower-http dependency remains on 0.6. This PR exposes the shared core with `no_std + alloc`, updates every direct Rust/npm dependency to its latest stable release, and adds enforced freshness checks.

- Add `merge` while preserving the existing feature-free core API. Result types, URL normalization, RRF with configurable `rrf_k`, weighted/interleave merging, and provider discovery compile without std.
- Export static metadata for all 40 providers, including categories, endpoint/body templates and capabilities. Server descriptors reuse the catalog; every existing provider, credential path, transport and default remains available.
- Make provider traversal, tied rankings, duplicate representatives and source lists deterministic. HashMap server callers and BTreeMap core consumers use the same algorithms.
- Refresh Cargo/npm manifests and lockfiles, including tower-http 0.7.1 and web-capture 0.3.37. Add tested freshness jobs for PRs, releases and weekly runs. Rust exceptions require an inline open-issue URL; JavaScript uses the documented manifest exception object because JSON cannot contain comments. Closed issues, PR URLs, empty explanations and unverifiable blockers fail.
- Prepare a Rust minor changelog fragment (0.6.0) and npm patch changeset (0.11.1) for the existing merge-triggered release workflows. Package publication remains pending maintainer merge.

The [complete requirement matrix, alternative components, research and solution plans](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/issue-27-9caaa1cdf786/docs/case-studies/issue-27/README.md) covers issues #25, #26 and #27, their comments, and the consumer audit. Prior PR #24 already isolated server dependencies, but the missing merge feature, std imports and inaccessible registry reproduced the remaining issue; no child issue was already fully resolved.

### Reproduction and regression coverage

Before the fix, the exact command below failed because `merge` did not exist. The new three-provider test also failed to compile against the old std-only merger and server-only registry.

```sh
cd rust
cargo build --no-default-features --features merge --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo test --no-default-features --features merge
cargo test --all-features
cargo outdated --root-deps-only --exit-code 1
```

`rust/tests/merge_core.rs` verifies known RRF scores, custom k/weights, all strategies, URL normalization, and identical HashMap/BTreeMap output. Registry tests verify every descriptor endpoint and preserve all 40 factories. The [standalone no_std consumer](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/tree/issue-27-9caaa1cdf786/rust/examples/no-std-consumer) compiles for both WASM and `thumbv7em-none-eabi`, proving the dependency graph works without the standard library.

### API and dependency changes

- tower-http 0.7 changes compression negotiation/quality types, removes no-op compression/Tokio features, makes trace/classification types non-exhaustive, and changes redirect extension handling. This crate only enables `cors`; its existing CorsLayer calls need no API adaptation and compile against 0.7.1.
- Changesets 3 uses ESM and newer Node/npm versions; its schema is updated and the existing `.mjs` release scripts remain compatible. lint-staged 17 also raises its Node requirement. Every JS workflow uses Node 24; published runtime support remains Node 20. Node 24's test runner rejects the former directory argument, so `npm test` now uses automatic discovery. The failure reproduced on Node 24.21.0 and the corrected command runs all 165 tests; a minimal before/after experiment is preserved in `experiments/node-test-discovery.mjs`.
- The server keeps HashMap weights; core-only weights use BTreeMap. Generic merger inputs may require a type annotation on previously ambiguous `collect()` calls. RegistryEntry struct literals must include the added endpoint/body/capability fields. The minor Rust release covers these additions and deterministic ordering.

### Validation and upstream limitation

Local validation passes: Rust all-feature tests (51 plus doctest), core-only tests (14 plus doctest), exact WASM build, both standalone no_std targets, warnings-denied Clippy/rustfmt, dependency boundary and size/package checks, eight Rust freshness tests, live registry freshness, cargo-outdated (exit 0), cargo update dry run (zero package updates), and JS/Rust parity. All 165 JavaScript tests pass under Node/Bun/Deno; lint, formatting, duplication, syntax, changeset status/validation, npm freshness and npm pack pass. npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities. Both version guards pass and origin/main is already an ancestor of this branch. Local large logs are preserved in ignored `ci-logs/`.

Final CI passes on `68641c36330f9fc24d7934605dcd1697cc6da40d` (runs created after the 2026-10-07 10:58:05 UTC commit): [full Rust CI](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/actions/runs/37611663654), [JavaScript CI](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/actions/runs/37610920060), and [JS/Rust parity](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/actions/runs/37611415550). Rust tests/doctests and JavaScript Node/Bun/Deno tests cover Linux/macOS/Windows; Rust CI also verifies the package build and core-only targets. Rust CI was explicitly dispatched on the branch because the existing per-commit detector otherwise skips the server matrix after a JavaScript-only commit. Automatic discovery additionally passes all 165 tests locally on Node 20, 24 and 26. The prior Node 24 directory-argument failure was reproduced, fixed and verified on every CI operating system. The working tree is clean and the fetched default branch is an ancestor.

The [independent consumer](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/tree/issue-27-9caaa1cdf786/experiments/tower-consumer) proves its direct tower-http and web-search share 0.7.1; its core-only graph has no duplicate packages. **The full-server no-duplicates acceptance check remains blocked upstream:** latest published Reqwest 0.13.5 unconditionally requires tower-http `^0.6.8`, while web-capture 0.3.37 and its Reqwest/browser stack also require 0.6. Cargo rejects forcing those dependencies to 0.7.1. [Reverse dependency evidence and the rejected update](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/tree/issue-27-9caaa1cdf786/docs/case-studies/issue-27/research) are included. Removing providers or adding a consumer-only patch would not meet the requested published-crate behavior. A compatible upstream release is needed to remove the final transitive copy.

title: Update tower-http to the latest release (0.6->0.7) and enforce dependency freshness in CI
body:
## Summary

Every dependency of this repository should be at its latest release (the maintainers' standing requirement, applied first in link-assistant/formal-ai#1169). The latest published `web-search` (0.5.0) and `rust/Cargo.toml` on `main` (checked 2026-09-29) declare dependencies whose latest release is outside the declared range:

| Dependency | Declared | Latest release |
|---|---|---|
| `tower-http` | 0.6 | 0.7.1 |

Consumers such as link-assistant/formal-ai compile a second copy of these crates next to the current ones, and cannot move to current versions of shared types.

## Requirements

1. R1: update every dependency in the table to its latest release and adapt the code to the new APIs (list each breaking change handled in the pull request description).
2. R2: run `cargo update` so the lockfile has no semver-compatible update pending (`cargo update --dry-run` prints no `Updating` lines).
3. R3: add a CI job that fails when a direct dependency is behind its latest release, unless the manifest line carries a comment with an open issue URL explaining the blocker. A ready-made form: `cargo install cargo-outdated --locked && cargo outdated --root-deps-only --exit-code 1` (for JavaScript packages in this repository: `npm outdated` exits 1 when anything is outdated).
4. R4: publish a release containing the updates (crates.io and npm where applicable).

## How to test

`cargo outdated --root-deps-only --exit-code 1` exits 0; `cargo tree -d` in a fresh crate that depends on this release and on the latest versions of the crates in the table shows no duplicates for them.

title: Offer RRF merging and the provider registry as a no_std + alloc feature for WASM consumers
body:
## Summary

The crate's reciprocal-rank-fusion merger (`rust/src/merger.rs`, `rrf_k`) and provider registry (`rust/src/providers/registry.rs`) are only available with `std` and the default `server` feature. Consumers that run in WASM re-implement both: link-assistant/formal-ai keeps `rust/src/web_search_core.rs` (753 lines: its own provider table, categories, per-category concurrency, `reciprocal_rank_fusion`, RRF input/output serialization) next to this dependency.

## What to do

- Split the pure parts into a `no_std` + `alloc` feature: result types, URL normalization, RRF and the other merge strategies, and the provider registry as data (name, category, endpoint template, capabilities).
- Export the provider registry so consumers can list and select providers without copying it.

## How to test

`cargo build --no-default-features --features merge --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds; a consumer can compute the same fused ranking as the server from three provider result lists.


---
Found by a duplication audit of link-assistant/formal-ai against the dependencies its maintainers own (consumer-side tracking: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1182; the audit table there lists the code this issue lets Formal AI delete). Per the organizations' policy, general logic belongs in the dependency so every consumer gets it out of the box and consumer code shrinks.

title: Expose caller-owned transport, cancellation, and provider outcomes
body:
## Summary

- add fetch-compatible JavaScript transports and a Rust `SearchTransport` trait across engine and built-in provider APIs
- propagate `AbortSignal` in JavaScript and keep Rust provider work within the aggregate future so dropping it cancels in-flight work
- add detailed searches with fused results plus independent success, error, or unavailable outcomes for every requested provider

title: Make merge-only use independent of server and capture dependencies
body:
## Downstream need

Formal AI now consumes `web-search` 0.3.1's published Rust result-merging API while retaining caller-owned fetching, cancellation, caching, errors, and provenance.

Although the crate declares `default = ["server"]`, the `server` feature is empty and the server/provider dependency graph is unconditional. Consequently, a merge-only consumer still compiles Axum, Reqwest, Tokio, and `web-capture`; the latter pulls the browser/native-TLS/OpenSSL stack. `default-features = false` therefore does not provide a lightweight library boundary.

This surfaced as an `openssl-sys` build failure in the downstream slim Docker builder: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/30779626456/job/91581726573

## Requested capability

Please make the existing `server` feature actually gate server-only modules and dependencies, and expose the deterministic merge types/functions under a lightweight library/core feature (or with no feature). A consumer selecting only the merge API should not compile Axum, Reqwest, Tokio, `web-capture`, or OpenSSL.

If registry/provider parsing can also be separated from network execution, caller-owned transport consumers could reuse more of the published component without losing exact status/body, cancellation, cache, and provenance semantics.

## Bounded downstream workaround

Formal AI is installing `pkg-config` and `libssl-dev` in its Docker builder only. The runtime image remains unchanged. Once a feature-gated release exists, it can disable the unused runtime graph and remove those builder packages.

Related downstream integration: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/912

title: Expose caller-owned transport, cancellation, and per-provider errors
body:
## Downstream need

Formal AI issue link-assistant/formal-ai#896 is adopting the published `web-search` component in production. Its source research path already has a content-addressed cache over exact response bytes, explicit transport/cache errors, and browser `AbortController` timeouts.

## Reproducer

The Rust `WebSearchEngine::search_with_options` owns provider transports and starts each provider with `tokio::spawn`; provider failures are converted to empty result lists. The JavaScript engine similarly uses `Promise.allSettled`, while providers either use global `fetch` or catch errors and return `[]`. Neither public search API accepts a caller-owned transport/`AbortSignal` or returns per-provider failure diagnostics.

As a result, replacing the downstream path with the engine directly would lose exact-byte cache provenance, caller cancellation, and the distinction between no results, cache miss, CAPTCHA, timeout, CORS, and transport failure.

## Requested capability

- Accept an injectable transport in both Rust and JavaScript public engine/provider APIs.
- Accept caller cancellation (`AbortSignal` in JS and a cancellation/future-lifetime contract in Rust).
- Return structured per-provider outcomes alongside fused results instead of reducing failures to empty lists.
- Preserve the exact response bytes or a capture receipt so downstream caches can bind rankings to their source.

## Bounded downstream workaround

Formal AI calls the published registry and `merger::merge_results`/`mergeResults` APIs, but keeps its existing cached transport, provider-response capture, cancellation, and diagnostics around that boundary. This can be removed when the component exposes the hooks above.

title: Bump to the latest version of https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture, rust, and other dependencies.
Make GitHub release tags short (rust-<v> / js-<v>) and fix missing npm/crates.io/GitHub releases
body:
## Summary

Closes #17. Makes GitHub release tags **short** — `rust-<version>` and `js-<version>` (no `v` prefix, single `-` separator) — and fixes the "I still don't see all the releases in package managers and GitHub" symptom by repairing three independent release-pipeline faults found while auditing the two runs the issue links to.

Full analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-17/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/issue-17-a319cc5b3fec/docs/case-studies/issue-17/README.md) and [`template-comparison.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/issue-17-a319cc5b3fec/docs/case-studies/issue-17/template-comparison.md).

## Release-channel state at investigation time

| Channel | Published | On `main` | Diagnosis |
|---|---|---|---|
| npm | `0.8.2` | `0.10.1` | bumped four releases ahead but never published |
| JS GitHub Releases | none | — | no JS release ever created |
| crates.io | `0.2.0` | `0.2.0` | crate version never advanced (no bump step) |
| Rust GitHub Releases | `0.2.0` ×2 | — | duplicate `rust-v` / `rust_v` tags for one version |

## Root causes & fixes

- **RC-1 — tag format (R1).** `getTagPrefix()` → `js-` (multi) / `''` (single); Rust workflow → `rust-$VERSION` / `$VERSION`. `normalizeVersion()` still strips every legacy spelling (`v`, `js-v`, `js_v`, `rust-v`, `rust_v`) so old tags remain valid inputs.
- **RC-2 — JS releases stuck (R3).** When `version-and-commit.mjs` finds nothing to commit (a prior run bumped + pushed but died before publishing, consuming the changeset), it now also sets `already_released=true`. The idempotent publish step then verifies npm and self-heals the missing version instead of skipping it forever. This is why npm sat at `0.8.2` while `package.json` was `0.10.1`.
- **RC-3 — Rust version never advances (R3).** The Rust release job had **no bump step**, so the crate was pinned at `0.2.0` forever. Added `get-bump-type.rs` / `bump-version.rs` / `collect-changelog.rs` (mirroring the JS changeset flow and the link-foundation rust template) and wired them into the release job: re-align to `origin/main` (concurrency-safe, no double-bump), pick the highest declared bump, rewrite `Cargo.toml`, fold `changelog.d/` fragments into `CHANGELOG.md`, `cargo update -p` the crate, commit `rust-<version>`, push, and target the release at the bump commit.
- **RC-4 — Rust publish was a false positive (R2).** The post-publish smoke test broke on a transitive `alloc-no-stdlib` 2.0.4/3.0.0 split (`E0277`) even though `0.2.0` was already published. The smoke test now collapses the duplicate major to 2.0.4 on the fresh consumer resolve (no-op once upstream realigns).
- **RC-5 — duplicate Rust tags (R2).** Tag convention centralised; the short scheme yields exactly one tag per version going forward. Existing duplicate `0.2.0` releases are left in place — deleting published releases is destructive/outward-facing, so the case study documents a manual cleanup recommendation instead.
- **R4/R9 — best practices / Node 20 deprecation.** Action pins bumped to Node 20+ runtimes (`checkout@v6`, `setup-node@v6`, `cache@v5`, `create-pull-request@v8`) across `js.yml`, `rust.yml`, `parity.yml`.

## What happens on the first push to `main` after merge

title: Fix CI/CD false positives so releases actually ship (issue #15)
body:
Fixes #15.

Makes the multi-language release pipeline actually ship — removes the CI false
positives, makes the Rust build deterministic, and corrects the GitHub-release
metadata. Full write-up: [`docs/case-studies/issue-15/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/issue-15-7e5742952426/docs/case-studies/issue-15/README.md).

## What was broken

| Pipeline | Symptom | Class |
| -------- | ------- | ----- |
| Rust | Smoke test aborted with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)` → exit 101 | **False positive** — healthy crate killed by the harness |
| Rust | `JS/Rust Parity` failed to compile `brotli`: `error[E0277]: StandardAlloc: alloc::Allocator<ZopfliNode> is not satisfied` | **Real, non-deterministic** — unpinned dep graph |
| JS | `Release` job: `ENEEDAUTH … requires you to be logged in` | **Owner config** — npm auth not provisioned |
| Both | Tags/titles/badges not namespaced per language; npm badge link malformed | **Correctness/UX** |

## Fixes in this PR

- **SIGPIPE smoke test (false positive).** `rust.yml` now captures
  `--list-providers` once and paginates the captured string instead of piping the
  live process into `head`. `rust/src/main.rs` renders the listing into one buffer
  and maps `BrokenPipe` → clean exit, so a closed reader never panics. Verified:
  `web-search --list-providers | head -n 5` now exits `0` (was `101`).
- **Deterministic Rust build.** `rust/Cargo.lock` was `.gitignore`d, so every CI
  run re-resolved deps; a freshly published `alloc-no-stdlib 3.0.0` split
  `brotli`'s allocator types on fresh resolution (the same commit passed at 00:41
  and failed at 09:34 with no source change). Fix: commit `Cargo.lock` (correct for
  a `[[bin]]` crate installed via `cargo install`; the rust template already keeps
  it committed) and unify on `alloc-no-stdlib 2.0.4` via `cargo update -p alloc-stdlib`.
- **Per-language release metadata.** Shared, unit-tested `js/scripts/release-naming.mjs`
  (21 tests) centralizes conventions: `js_v…`/`rust_v…` tags (was `js-v`/`rust-v`),
  `[JavaScript] …`/`[Rust] …` titles, and a package-manager shields badge in the
  release body linking to the exact published version. Single- vs multi-language
  layout is auto-detected (`getJsRoot()` for JS; `[ -f Cargo.toml ]` for Rust).
- **Case study + upstream reports.** `docs/case-studies/issue-15/` holds the
  timeline, root-cause analysis, template comparison, raw CI logs, and
  ready-to-file `upstream-reports.md` for the genuinely shared template gaps.

## Remaining owner action (not a code bug)

JS publish fails with `ENEEDAUTH` because neither auth path is provisioned for
`@link-assistant/web-search`: set the `NPM_TOKEN` secret **or** configure an OIDC
trusted publisher on npmjs.org. The JS release job is already correctly wired for
both; once either exists, the pending `0.10.0` publishes with no code change.

```
target/debug/web-search --list-providers | head -n 5   # exits 0
cd ../js && node --test tests/                          # 155 pass
npm run check                                           # eslint + prettier + jscpd
cd .. && node js/scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs       # parity passed
```

title: FormalAI adoption blocker: publish web-search packages (self-healing release, versioned docs, smoke tests)
body:
## Summary

Resolves the FormalAI adoption blocker in #6: make `web-search` reliably
consumable as a **published package** in both ecosystems, and prove it stays
that way.

Both packages are already published (npm `@link-assistant/web-search@0.8.2`,
crates.io `web-search@0.2.0`), so the issue's original `E404`/not-found symptom
is stale. The remaining, still-live problems were: the JS release automation
could get **stuck** (a failed publish consumes its changeset, so the next push
skips), the README install docs were **unversioned**, and CI only checked that a
version was **indexed**, never that it was **installable**. This PR fixes all
three and reports the shared CI/CD gap upstream.

Full analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-6/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/issue-6-9ad68b60fc91/docs/case-studies/issue-6/README.md).

## Acceptance criteria (issue #6)

| Criterion | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Publish `@link-assistant/web-search` to npm | ✅ Published (`0.8.2`); release now **self-heals** so a stuck version (`0.9.0`) republishes |
| Publish the Rust crate to crates.io | ✅ `web-search@0.2.0` published; pipeline works |
| Release tags / GitHub releases mapping to versions | ✅ `rust-v0.2.0` exists; JS publishes create `js-v<version>` going forward |
| Document library/CLI/HTTP entry points with **versioned** install commands | ✅ README *Entry points* table + versioned npm/cargo commands |
| CI exercises **install-from-package smoke tests** after publication | ✅ npm + crates.io smoke tests added |
| Compare CI/CD vs the 4 templates; report shared issues upstream | ✅ 4 issues filed (js#81, rust#73, python#20, csharp#27) |
| Download logs/data + compile a case study | ✅ `docs/case-studies/issue-6/` |

## Changes

**Release reliability (root cause: stuck `0.9.0`)**
- `js/scripts/check-release-needed.mjs` — self-healing detection that checks
  **npm (source of truth), not git tags**; republishes an unpublished version
  when no changeset exists. Wired into `.github/workflows/js.yml` with an
  expanded publish condition.

**Install-from-package smoke tests (root cause: "indexed" ≠ "installable")**
- `js/scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs` — installs the published npm package into a
  clean temp project (with propagation retries) and verifies the **library**,
  **CLI** (`--list-providers`), and **HTTP server** (`serve` → `/health`).
- `rust.yml` — a `Smoke-test published crate` step that `cargo install`s the
  crate from crates.io, runs the binary, and compiles a fresh dependent crate.

**Documentation + CLI parity**
- README: *Entry points* table + versioned `npm install …@0.9.0` /
  `cargo add …@0.2.0` / `cargo install` commands.
- Added a `serve` subcommand to the JS CLI (`web-search serve --port <port>`) as
  a parity alias for `--serve`, matching the Rust CLI. Exported `parseArgs` and
  guarded the auto-run so the parser is unit-testable.
- `js/tests/cli.test.js` — covers `--serve`, the `serve` subcommand, and that a
  query containing "serve" is not misinterpreted.

**Case study + upstream reports**
- `docs/case-studies/issue-6/` — timeline, root-cause analysis, template
  comparison, raw logs/data, and the 4 filed upstream issue bodies.

## How to reproduce / verify

```bash
cd js
npm install
npm test                                   # 134 tests incl. cli.test.js
npm run check                              # eslint + script syntax + prettier + jscpd

# Self-healing: no changesets, version ahead of npm → should_release=true, skip_bump=true
HAS_CHANGESETS=false node js/scripts/check-release-needed.mjs --js-root js

# Install-from-package smoke test (CI runs after publish; locally needs a published version)
node js/scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs --package-version 0.8.2 --js-root js
```

## Remaining owner action

Subsequent npm publishes need either the `NPM_TOKEN` secret set, or a configured
OIDC trusted publisher on npmjs.org for the now-existing package (a brand-new
package cannot be bootstrapped by OIDC). The pipeline self-heals once auth is
available.

Closes #6.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the CI/CD false positives that prevented `link-assistant/web-search` from
actually publishing releases to npm + crates.io and creating GitHub Releases.
Closes #11.

Both release jobs referenced in the issue failed on the **same commit**
(`c67aef6`, the merge of PR #10). Every other job passed — the failures were
isolated to the publish/release jobs that talk to external registries.

A full reconstruction (timeline, requirements matrix, root causes, template
comparison, and evidence) is in
[`docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/issue-11-319b016aadbe/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md).

## Root causes & fixes

| # | Root cause (evidence) | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RC1 | crates.io returns **HTTP 403** without a `User-Agent`; the old inline `curl -fsS` defeated the publish-skip on every run (`curl: (22) … error: 403` in the Rust log) | Pre-flight check now sends `curl -A …`; 200→skip publish, 404→publish, else→hard error |
| RC2 | `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` was empty at publish time (`##[error]CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN is required`) | Job-level `env` maps `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN \|\| secrets.CARGO_TOKEN`; publishing delegated to `publish-crate.rs` (template parity) with failure classification + deferred rate-limit |
| RC3 | npm **OIDC trusted publishing cannot bootstrap a brand-new package** → `E404 … PUT …@link-assistant%2fweb-search` | Both publish steps pass `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: secrets.NPM_TOKEN` as an optional first-publish bootstrap; OIDC still used once the package exists. Publish jobs on Node `24.x` |
| RC4 | Permanent E404/auth failures were retried 3× and surfaced as a generic error | `publish-to-npm.mjs` classifies non-retryable failures and exits immediately with actionable guidance |
| RC5 | GitHub Release creation was not idempotent → red on re-run over an existing tag | Idempotent in both languages (`gh release view` guard / `already_exists` treated as success) |

## Requirement coverage (issue #11)

- **R1** Fix false positives so releases actually publish — ✅ all five root causes above.
- **R2** Compare against the four `link-foundation` templates and reuse best practices — ✅ Rust `publish-crate.rs` / `wait-for-crate.rs` / `setup-npm.mjs` adopted verbatim; comparison table in the case study.
- **R3 / R6** Report shared bugs upstream — ✅ filed [js-template #77](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/77) (retry classification + first-publish bootstrap). The crates.io 403 bug is **repo-specific** (the template already sends a User-Agent).
- **R4** Download logs/data + deep case study — ✅ `docs/case-studies/issue-11/`.
- **R5** Add debug/verbose if data was insufficient — not needed; logs were conclusive and the publish scripts already emit verbose, actionable diagnostics.
- **R7** Apply fixes everywhere — ✅ both JS publish paths (release + instant-release) and the Rust release job.
- **R8** Single PR — ✅ this PR.

## Verification

- JS: `120/120` tests, `eslint`, `prettier --check` (incl. workflows), `jscpd`, `check:scripts`, JS/Rust parity — all pass.
- Rust: `cargo fmt --check`, `publish-crate.rs` (7 tests) + `wait-for-crate.rs` (2 tests), file-size check — all pass.
- Live registry probes confirming the root causes are recorded in `docs/case-studies/issue-11/research/live-registry-probes.txt`.

## ⚠️ Maintainer action required (secrets cannot be set by automation)

- **Rust:** set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (or `CARGO_TOKEN`) to a crates.io publish token.
- **JS (first release only):** set `NPM_TOKEN` to an npm automation token to bootstrap the first publish of `@link-assistant/web-search`. After that, configure a trusted publisher on npmjs.com and the token becomes optional.

A JS changeset and a Rust changelog fragment are included to trigger the next patch release once merged.

title: FormalAI adoption blocker: align provider parity and defaults
body:
FormalAI issue link: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/410

During the FormalAI issue 410 case study, I compared FormalAI's current `src/web_search_core.rs` provider contract with `web-search` HEAD.

Current gaps:

- FormalAI's live default plan is `duckduckgo`, `internet-archive`, `wikipedia`, `wikidata`, `wiktionary`, `wikinews`.
- `web-search` currently reports default providers as `duckduckgo`, `google`, `bing`, `wikipedia`.
- The registry metadata marks Google as `defaultForCategory: true` and DuckDuckGo as `defaultForCategory: false`, while FormalAI currently treats DuckDuckGo as the default search provider.
- `web-search` does not yet include several FormalAI provider IDs, including `internet-archive`, `wiktionary`, `wikinews`, `openlibrary`, `semantic-scholar`, `europepmc`, `doaj`, `dbpedia`, the dictionary providers, `yandex`, and the non-GitHub code hosts (`gitlab`, `codeberg`, `gitee`, `bitbucket`, `gitflic`).

Why this blocks FormalAI:

Replacing FormalAI's current in-repo registry with `web-search` right now would remove existing provider coverage and would change the default search semantics. FormalAI issue 410 asks to use `web-search` as the component, but it also asks to make sure the component has all supported/required features first.

Requested acceptance criteria:

- Make `web-search` a superset of FormalAI's current provider IDs or provide a documented compatibility map for provider IDs that intentionally differ.
- Align default search semantics with FormalAI's DuckDuckGo-first behavior, or document a migration plan that FormalAI can opt into explicitly.
- Include FormalAI's current live default plan: DuckDuckGo, Internet Archive, Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wiktionary, and Wikinews.
- Add provider-registry tests in JavaScript and Rust that assert FormalAI-compatible IDs, categories, CORS/fetchability metadata, and defaults.
- Keep the optional `web-capture` provider namespace, but make clear which providers are native search providers and which are delegated through capture.

title: Issue #3: support both Rust and JavaScript with full provider parity
body:
## Summary

Fully implements issue #3 — **web-search now ships as two first-class
implementations, JavaScript and Rust, kept in lock-step parity.** Both languages
expose the same descriptor-driven provider catalog, the same typed registry over
the four `formal-ai` categories, the same merge strategies, and the same CLI/HTTP
surface. `--list-providers` reports an identical **22 providers** in both
languages (search 15, knowledge 2, papers 3, code 2).

## What changed

### Dual-language provider catalog (parity)
- **Descriptor-driven engines** declared as data (id, request kind, parser) run
  through a single shared `GenericProvider` — adding an engine in one place adds
  it everywhere. Mirrored in `src/providers/` (JS) and `rust/src/providers/` (Rust).
- **Shared HTML utilities**: entity decoding, tag stripping, and a generic
  anchor-list parser, aligned byte-for-byte across languages (incl.
  `…`/`—`/`–`).
- **Typed provider registry** — a single source of truth powering discovery
  (`--list-providers`, `/providers`, `/providers?category=`, `/categories`) and
  factory instantiation.

### Providers (22 total, four `formal-ai` categories)
- `search` (15): google, bing, duckduckgo, searx, brave, mojeek, ecosia,
  startpage, yahoo, lite (DuckDuckGo Lite), and 5 `wc:*` web-capture providers
- `knowledge` (2): wikipedia, wikidata
- `papers` (3): crossref, openalex, arxiv
- `code` (2): github, hackernews

### web-capture as a component library
- The optional `@link-assistant/web-capture` library backs the `wc:*` providers.
  It is loaded lazily and degrades gracefully (warn-once + empty results) when not
  installed, so the rest of the aggregation keeps working.

### Tests, docs, release
- **115 JS tests** (`node --test tests/`) and Rust integration suites for the
  registry (8), HTML utilities (5), and every parser (10), plus unit + doc tests.
- README rewritten around categories, access types, the descriptor catalog, the
  web-capture component, and the registry.
- Deep case study compiled in `docs/case-studies/issue-3/`.
- Changeset added (`minor`); Rust crate bumped to `0.2.0`.

## How to verify

```bash
# JavaScript
node --test tests/           # 115 pass
npm run check                # eslint + prettier + jscpd
node bin/web-search.js --list-providers

# Rust
cd rust
cargo fmt --check
RUSTFLAGS="-Dwarnings" cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
cargo test && cargo test --doc
./target/release/web-search --list-providers   # same 22 providers
```

## Requirements mapping (issue #3)
- **R1** Rust + JavaScript as first-class implementations — ✅ full parity, verified by `--list-providers`
- **R2/R3** adopt web-capture best practices and use it as a **component library** — ✅ `wc:*` providers, lazy + graceful degrade
- **R4** web-capture covers protocols/interfaces — ✅ exposed through the descriptor/registry contract
- **R5** features required by `formal-ai` — ✅ four-category registry, RRF (k=60), discovery endpoints
- **R6** reuse link-foundation CI/CD best practices — ✅ changesets, lint/format/duplication gates, Rust CI (fmt/clippy -Dwarnings/test/doc)
- **R7** deep case study — ✅ `docs/case-studies/issue-3/`
- **R8** single PR — ✅ this PR

Closes #3
